text: According to endurantism (three-dimensionalism), how does an object persist through time?
choices: By having a distinct temporal part at each moment, which together compose a four-dimensional whole
By being wholly present at each moment of its existence, without having any temporal parts
By being an instantaneous stage that stands in a temporal counterpart relation to earlier and later stages
By never really persisting at all, since 'sameness over time' is a fiction the mind projects onto distinct things
explanation: Endurantism holds that an object is wholly present at every moment it exists, with no temporal parts — which is why it is called three-dimensionalism. The temporal-parts option describes perdurantism (the four-dimensional temporal-worm view); the counterpart-relation option describes Sider's stage theory; and the 'fiction' option is a Humean deflationism about identity. Only wholly-present persistence is endurantism.
